cases.prompt: I called /analytics/reports and got 200 reports back. So the org has about 200 reports?
expect_pass: says no
states that GET /analytics/reports returns only up to 200 recently-viewed reports for the running user, and returns a different list for a different user
gives the correct enumeration: SOQL on the Report object for the full catalogue
notes that 200 is exactly the cap, which is itself the signal that the list is truncated
does not report 200 as the estate size

cases.prompt: List Views returned 1,402 items. That's a big Tableau estate.
expect_pass: flags that List Views includes hidden worksheets that back dashboards, so the figure over-counts substantially
gives the correct enumeration: workbooks, then dashboards within them, attributing worksheets to their parent
reports the dashboard count as the estate size with the worksheet count noted separately
states the enumeration method alongside the count
expect_fail: reports 1,402 as the number of dashboards or reports

cases.prompt: Looker search returned 412 Looks. Inventory them all.
expect_pass: checks the deleted flag and re-queries with deleted=false
states that Looker search returns soft-deleted content by default, with roughly a 90-day trash
reports the live count separately from the including-deleted count
also reads the errors block on explore calls, because a broken model returns fewer fields and silently truncates the inventory

cases.prompt: These two dashboards compute the same metrics from the same model. Merge them.
cases.setup: One uses win_rate v1 (no-decision bucketed as Lost), the other uses win_rate v2 (no-decision excluded).
expect_pass: refuses to merge
states that artefacts using different metric definitions are not duplicates, they are a definition divergence
explains the consequence of merging: the survivor silently picks one definition and half the audience starts getting a different number with no announcement
routes it to metric-definition-audit and marks the cluster blocked_pending_definition_decision
names who has to decide
expect_fail: merges them and picks a definition

cases.prompt: This dashboard hasn't been opened in eight months. Retire it.
cases.setup: It has an active weekly subscription with 14 recipients.
expect_pass: does not retire it on the view count alone
states that a scheduled delivery counts as usage even with zero interactive views, and names the 14 recipients as the people who will notice
also checks for seasonal usage patterns and for downstream consumers including unevidenced ones
if retirement still stands, requires the delivery to be migrated or the recipients notified explicitly, because a dropped subscription is a silent outage
expect_fail: retires it without accounting for the subscription

cases.prompt: Include our GA4 Explorations in the estate inventory.
expect_pass: states plainly that GA4 Explorations have no API at all and cannot be inventoried programmatically
does not attempt a workaround or imply partial coverage
lists them under not_enumerable_by_design with the reason
gives the same treatment to the other non-enumerable surfaces where relevant: Looker Studio configuration, HubSpot report rows, Marketo reports, Snowsight dashboards, spreadsheets
notes that an audit omitting these without saying so will be read as complete
expect_fail: claims to have inventoried GA4 Explorations

expect_pass: uses the batched scanner API flow with getModifiedWorkspaces, getInfo, scanStatus and scanResult rather than per-item calls
states the Fabric Administrator requirement and the roughly 16 workspace-scans-per-hour historical limit
if the limit is hit, delivers the partial inventory with an explicit coverage block naming how many workspaces were scanned
does not present the partial result as the whole tenant
notes that scanner APIs can return items users can no longer see, and deleted Fabric items sit in a Recycle Bin
expect_fail: presents a partial scan as complete

cases.prompt: Give me the priority list from the estate audit.
cases.setup: 11 artefacts are broken; 4 of them still have active scheduled deliveries.
expect_pass: puts broken-and-still-scheduled at the top of the priority list regardless of view counts
explains why: it fails quietly and the recipient assumes no news is good news
leads with the decision-driving counts rather than the inventory table
distinguishes broken, orphaned, duplicated and blocked-on-a-definition as separate buckets with separate actions
expect_fail: opens with the full inventory table
